packageRules.description: An action update is executable code, not a version string: every workflow in this factory runs actions with contents: write, packages: write and id-token: write, so a bumped ref runs with the tokens that sign and publish our RPMs the moment it lands. Unlike a build-root digest, a rotted action pin does not fail the run -- it just runs something else -- so automerging buys no availability and spends the only review this supply chain gets. A human reads the diff. Stated explicitly rather than left to the top-level default, so a preset bump cannot re-enable it unnoticed.
Direct upstream RPM sources may merge only after their real build and verification gate succeeds.

A build-root image digest may move on its own: a rotted pin fails every job in the run, and the replacement is whatever the pinned tag already resolves to. Digest only -- a new Fedora major is a deliberate decision.

customManagers.description: Every factory RPM source is tracked at its actual upstream, rather than Fedora Rawhide or dist-git.

Container images named inside a workflow run: script. Renovate's docker manager reads Dockerfiles, container: and services:, none of which covers an image passed to docker run in a shell line -- so these pins were tracked by nothing and rotted twice in a week, each time taking every job in the run down with exit 125 before a line of its script ran (quay.io/fedora/fedora, and quay.io/packit/packit on two separate digests). The tag is written alongside the digest so this can resolve what to track: fedora follows :44, not :latest.
